THE READ

Quantified ML results and system scale are unusually strong; leadership and operational details remain uneven.

WHAT LANDS

The two-stage ranking architecture connects candidate generation and learned re-ranking to 11 percent more weekly watch time, 6 percent higher subscription conversion, and flat infrastructure cost.

WHERE DOUBT CREEPS IN

The resume shows what you improved, but gives little detail on experiment design, rollout decisions, or how you separated model effects from other changes.

OTHER LINE REWRITES

Useful edits, kept with their own source.

These do not map uniquely to the ranked fixes above, so each stays beside the exact line it rewrites.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“Drove fairness and quality reviews for personalization models, tightening guardrails on extreme content and establishing a quarterly model audit process with Legal and Policy.”

REWRITE

Drove fairness and quality reviews for personalization models, tightening guardrails on extreme content and establishing a quarterly model audit process with Legal and Policy; scope: [specific scope]; outcome: [measurable result].

Add the number of models, review findings, or launch decisions affected to show what the audit process changed.

LINE EDIT 02 · SOURCE LINE

“Mentored a team of 6 ML engineers and 3 data scientists, driving a culture of clear experiment design, readable dashboards, and defensible decision memos.”

REWRITE

Mentored a team of 6 ML engineers and 3 data scientists by setting expectations for experiment design, readable dashboards, and defensible decision memos; [team or delivery improvement].

Add one verified change in team practice, delivery cadence, or decision quality to make the mentoring work concrete.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

When did watch time and subscription conversion move differently, and how did you choose the ranking tradeoff?

Why it may help: Your ranking work reports both measures, but the decision tension between them is not visible.

QUESTION 02

What changed in the architecture or operating model to serve a 200M monthly active user platform?

Why it may help: The user scale is clear; the engineering choices that made it workable would sharpen the Staff-level story.

QUESTION 03

Describe a personalization incident where guardrails, latency, or model quality forced a difficult production decision.

Why it may help: The resume names monitoring and fairness reviews, but not a concrete high-pressure judgment.

QUESTION 04

Which part of the offline evaluation harness removed the most iteration time from weeks to days?

Why it may help: The time reduction is strong, and explaining the mechanism would make the improvement more transferable.

QUESTION 05

How did Legal and Policy change the quarterly personalization audit process or its launch decisions?

Why it may help: The partnership is named, but the practical consequence of that collaboration is not stated.

KEEP THESE

The parts already earning trust.
01

The two-stage ranking architecture connects candidate generation and learned re-ranking to 11 percent more weekly watch time, 6 percent higher subscription conversion, and flat infrastructure cost.

02

The ads quality role links calibrated probabilities and down-funnel metrics to an estimated 22 million dollars per year in net new revenue, which makes the business value easy to understand.

03

The career progression from demand forecasting to ads quality to personalization shows a consistent production ML path across retail, advertising, and streaming.

ROLE DIRECTION

Where this story reads strongest.

Position yourself around large-scale ranking and recommendation systems with unusually clear business and infrastructure results. For Staff or Principal ML roles, bring the leadership decisions and cross-functional operating model closer to the foreground.

BEST FIT NOW

report.biggest_gap_example: "Maintained model performance and data pipelines in production, including monitoring, retraining, and incident response." lacks scale or a concrete incident result, so the operational burden is hard to judge.
report.first_impression: This is an unusually quantitative Staff ML resume, with recommendation, ads, and forecasting work tied to user, revenue, and infrastructure results. The stray "javascript" entry and a few less-specific leadership bullets interrupt an otherwise clear senior-level read.
gaps: The resume shows what you improved, but gives little detail on experiment design, rollout decisions, or how you separated model effects from other changes.
The leadership bullets describe mentoring and reviews without showing the decisions you made, the audiences involved, or the resulting change in team or model practice.
The recent work is concentrated at Nimbus, so the resume gives limited context on organizational scale, product constraints, or ownership beyond the listed systems.

report.score_comment_long: The recent work is dense with scale and results: 200M monthly active users, 1B plus daily ad requests, revenue growth, and latency reductions. A few bullets still describe leadership or operations without showing what changed afterward. Tightening those lines and removing the stray skills entry would make the resume easier to trust at a higher Staff or Principal bar.
report.score_comment_short: Quantified ML results and system scale are unusually strong; leadership and operational details remain uneven.
report.score_plain: This resume should compete well for Staff ML roles in ranking, recommendations, ads, and ML infrastructure. The remaining edits mainly determine whether a reviewer sees broad technical leadership or mainly excellent individual projects.

Education.fix: No change needed unless it improves role alignment.
Education.working: Both degrees are relevant, and the machine learning focus is stated directly.

Skills.fix: Remove the standalone "javascript" entry and keep the taxonomy consistent, including "A B testing" as "A/B testing" if accurate.
Skills.missing: The section does not show proficiency or recency, and the stray entry looks like an editing artifact.
Skills.working: The tools are grouped sensibly across languages, ML, systems, domains, and practices.

Summary.fix: Replace broad claims such as "Strong at partnering" with one compact example tied to ranking, revenue, or infrastructure.
Summary.missing: The summary does not distinguish your technical leadership decisions from your collaboration responsibilities.
Summary.working: It identifies Staff-level ML, recommendation and ranking focus, user scale, and business outcomes.

Work Experience.fix: Add one verified result or operating detail to the mentoring, audit, and production-maintenance bullets.
Work Experience.missing: A few bullets lack a concrete consequence, despite the surrounding roles being highly quantified.
Work Experience.working: The experience section gives clear progression and several excellent mechanism-to-result examples.

strengths: The two-stage ranking architecture connects candidate generation and learned re-ranking to 11 percent more weekly watch time, 6 percent higher subscription conversion, and flat infrastructure cost.
The ads quality role links calibrated probabilities and down-funnel metrics to an estimated 22 million dollars per year in net new revenue, which makes the business value easy to understand.
The career progression from demand forecasting to ads quality to personalization shows a consistent production ML path across retail, advertising, and streaming.
report.summary: The clearest value here is production ML at meaningful scale: recommendation systems for 200M monthly active users, ads models handling 1B plus daily requests, and forecasting across three product categories. Your progression supports Staff-level individual contributor roles, with technical leadership shown through architecture changes, infrastructure partnerships, and mentoring 6 ML engineers plus 3 data scientists. The main question is how your governance, mentoring, and incident work changed decisions or team performance, which affects the case for Principal-level breadth. That part works: the business results are specific enough to keep the resume grounded.
